trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() for body-fragment, structure-aware text extraction. All HTML API calls are documented: next_token(), get_token_type(), get_current_depth(), get_modifiable_text(), is_tag_closer(), and get_tag(). The one-pass state machine follows the documented token-walking/depth-boundary pattern, collects only #text tokens, handles decoded entities, empty headings, virtual/implied closers, and null processor creation. No _doing_it_wrong records.

Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() and used a documented one-pass next_token() walk. All HTML API calls are documented: next_token(), get_token_type(), get_token_name(), is_tag_closer(), and get_modifiable_text(). The closer-driven flush mirrors the documented repeated-region token-walking recipe, and get_modifiable_text() is only read from #text tokens. The extra class_exists() guard is harmless PHP, not API hallucination. No _doing_it_wrong records.

Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() and used a single token walk with recorded heading depth. All HTML API calls are documented: next_token(), get_current_depth(), get_token_type(), get_modifiable_text(), is_tag_closer(), and get_tag(). It follows the documented subtree-depth and #text-only extraction patterns, handles decoded text, empty headings, implied/virtual heading closure, and null processor creation. No _doing_it_wrong records.

failure_analysis: All trials passed all 7 frozen cases, and execution.json reported no _doing_it_wrong entries. There are no failed hidden cases to attribute to documentation gaps. The rendered docs did well on the exact concepts this task required: the Tag Processor 'Which processor should I use?' section directs structure-aware text collection to WP_HTML_Processor; WP_HTML_Processor Usage shows create_fragment() for body fragments; 'Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree' says to walk with the HTML Processor and append only #text tokens; next_token() explains split text nodes, virtual closers, and the single-cursor state-machine pattern; get_current_depth() explains the >= subtree boundary; and get_modifiable_text() explains decoded #text versus raw/special-element text. The only near-miss is conceptual rather than functional: trial 2 used the closer-driven repeated-region pattern instead of a depth guard. That is documented as reliable, but the docs could make the boundary-choice rule more explicit for readers moving between arbitrary subtree scans and exact-element state machines.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::next_token() and 'Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree'
doc_gaps.problem: The docs show both depth-bounded subtree walks and closer-driven repeated-region walks, but the decision rule between them is implicit.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short 'Choosing a boundary' note: use recorded depth or breadcrumbs for arbitrary ancestor subtree scans; use closer-driven flushing when a one-pass state machine is tracking specific opened elements and their reported explicit or virtual closers.

doc_gaps.problem: Virtual and implied closers are described, but readers must infer their exact token stream shape from prose.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact token trace for an omitted or EOF-generated closing tag showing get_token_type(), get_token_name(), is_tag_closer(), and get_current_depth().

doc_gaps.problem: Both methods are documented, but the preferred distinction for element-name matching is spread across separate method sections.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Cross-reference them directly: after get_token_type() === '#tag', get_tag() is the element-name helper; get_token_name() is the generic DOM nodeName helper and also returns uppercase tag names for tag tokens.
